ja: コンピューターのマウスは1964年ごろダグラス・エンゲルバートが考えた。最初のマウスは木の箱だった。
easy: The computer mouse was made in the 1960s by Douglas Engelbart. The first one was a small wooden box.
std: Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in the 1960s; the first prototype was a wooden box with two wheels.

ja: 水泳のバタフライは、平泳ぎのルールのすき間から生まれた。腕を水の上で戻すことが禁止されていなかったため。
easy: The butterfly swimming style began as a new way to do the breaststroke. The rules did not stop swimmers from moving their arms above the water.
std: The butterfly stroke grew out of a loophole in breaststroke rules, which did not forbid bringing the arms forward over the water.

ja: 白黒模様のサッカーボールは、1970年のW杯で白黒テレビでも見やすいように使われて広まった。
easy: The black and white football became popular at the 1970 World Cup. It was easy to see on black and white TV.
std: The classic black-and-white football became famous at the 1970 World Cup, partly because it was easy to see on black-and-white television.

ja: テニスの点数が「15、30、40」と数えるのは、時計の文字盤から来たという説がある（はっきりとは分かっていない）。
easy: Nobody is sure why tennis scores go 15, 30, 40. One idea is that they come from the face of a clock.
std: No one knows for certain why tennis is scored 15, 30, 40; one popular theory links it to the quarters of a clock face.

ja: バスケットボールは1891年、体育教師のジェームズ・ネイスミスが冬に室内でできる運動として考えた。
easy: Basketball was made in 1891 by a teacher who wanted a sport to play inside in winter.
std: Basketball was invented in 1891 by physical education teacher James Naismith as an indoor game for the winter months.

ja: 19世紀のボクシングでは、ラウンドの数に決まりがなく、どちらかが続けられなくなるまで試合が続いた。
easy: In the 1800s, a boxing match could go on until one fighter could not go on.
std: Under 19th-century bare-knuckle rules, boxing matches had no set number of rounds and continued until one fighter could not go on.

ja: マラソンの42.195kmは、1908年のロンドン五輪で、ウィンザー城からスタジアムのロイヤルボックス前までのコースにしたことから決まった。
easy: The marathon became 42.195 km long at the 1908 London Olympics because of where the race started and ended.
std: The marathon's 42.195 km distance comes from the 1908 London Olympics, where the course ran from Windsor Castle to the royal box in the stadium.

ja: ゴルフボールのくぼみ（ディンプル）は空気の流れを変え、つるつるのボールよりずっと遠くまで飛ばす。
easy: The small holes on a golf ball help it fly much farther than a smooth ball.
std: The dimples on a golf ball change how air flows around it, letting it fly much farther than a smooth ball.

ja: 大相撲の番付は18世紀半ばから続く、とても歴史の長いランキングのしくみ。
easy: Sumo has used the same kind of ranking list for more than 250 years.
std: Sumo's banzuke ranking list dates back to the mid-18th century, making it one of the oldest sports rankings in use.

ja: アメフトの「ハドル」は、19世紀末にろう者の大学のチームが、相手に手話を見られないように始めたとされる。
easy: In American football, players stand in a circle to plan. This may have started at a school for deaf students, so other teams could not see their signs.
std: The football huddle is said to have begun at Gallaudet University, a school for deaf students, so opponents could not read their sign language.

ja: スキーは数千年前の北ヨーロッパで、狩りや移動のために使われていた。スポーツとして広まったのは19世紀。
easy: People in the north of Europe used skis thousands of years ago to hunt and travel. Skiing became a sport in the 1800s.
std: Skis were used for hunting and travel in northern Europe thousands of years ago; skiing became a sport only in the 19th century.

ja: マイケル・フェルプスは2008年北京五輪で金メダルを8個とった。1大会での最多記録。
easy: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at the 2008 Olympics. No one has won more at one Games.
std: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the most ever at a single Games.

ja: 大リーグの試合球は、試合の前に特別な川の泥をすりこんで、すべりにくくしている。
easy: Before a baseball game in the US, each ball is rubbed with special mud from a river.
std: Before every Major League Baseball game, the balls are rubbed with a special mud from a river in New Jersey to reduce their shine.

ja: 円周率πは終わりなく続く数。これまでに小数点以下100兆けた以上が計算されている。
easy: Pi is a number that never ends. Computers have worked out more than 100 trillion numbers after the point.
std: Pi is an irrational number whose digits never end; computers have calculated it to more than 100 trillion decimal places.

ja: 数としての「0」を使う考え方は、7世紀ごろのインドで整えられ、アラビアを通ってヨーロッパに伝わった。
easy: The idea of zero as a number came from India and later went to Europe through the Arab world.
std: Zero as a number in its own right was developed in India around the 7th century and reached Europe through the Arab world.

ja: フィボナッチ数列（1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…）は、ひまわりの種の並びなど、自然の中によく現れる。
easy: The numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 are called the Fibonacci numbers. You can find them in many plants, like sunflowers.
std: The Fibonacci sequence (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13...) appears often in nature, such as in the spiral patterns of sunflower seeds.

ja: 「誕生日のパラドックス」：23人集まれば、同じ誕生日の2人がいる確率は50%を超える。
easy: If there are 23 people in a room, there is a better than even chance that two of them have the same birthday.
std: In a group of just 23 people, there is more than a 50% chance that two share a birthday, the so-called birthday paradox.

ja: 無限にも「大きさ」の違いがある。実数の無限は、自然数の無限より大きい（カントール）。
easy: Some kinds of 'never ending' are bigger than others. A mathematician named Cantor showed this.
std: Georg Cantor showed that some infinities are larger than others: there are more real numbers than natural numbers.

ja: コンピューターは0と1だけの2進法で計算する。2進法を詳しく研究したのは17〜18世紀のライプニッツ。
easy: Computers work using only 0 and 1. A thinker named Leibniz wrote about this way of counting long ago.
std: Computers calculate using binary, just 0s and 1s, a number system studied in depth by Gottfried Leibniz around 1700.

ja: 「フェルマーの最終定理」は350年以上だれにも証明できなかったが、1995年にアンドリュー・ワイルズが証明を完成させた。
easy: A famous math problem waited more than 350 years for an answer. Andrew Wiles solved it in 1995.
std: Fermat's Last Theorem remained unproven for over 350 years until Andrew Wiles completed his proof in 1995.

ja: バタフライ効果：最初のわずかな違いが、天気のような複雑なしくみでは大きな違いになる。天気予報に限界がある理由のひとつ。
easy: In weather, a very small change can lead to a very big change later. This is why weather is hard to know far ahead.
std: In chaotic systems such as the weather, tiny differences in starting conditions grow into huge differences, which limits long-range forecasts.

ja: モンティ・ホール問題：3つのドアから1つ選び、はずれのドアを1つ開けてもらったら、選び直したほうが当たる確率は2/3になる。
easy: In a game with three doors, if one wrong door is opened, you should change your choice. You will win two times out of three.
std: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doors after a losing door is revealed wins two thirds of the time.

ja: インターネットの安全を守る暗号の多くは、大きな数を素数に分けるのが難しいことを利用している。
easy: Much of the safety on the internet depends on special numbers called prime numbers.
std: Much internet security relies on public-key cryptography, which depends on how hard it is to break large numbers into prime factors.

ja: 「ケーニヒスベルクの橋」の問題（1736年）を考えたことから、オイラーはグラフ理論の土台を作った。
easy: A puzzle about seven bridges in an old city led Euler to start a new kind of math.
std: Leonhard Euler's 1736 solution to the Seven Bridges of Königsberg puzzle laid the foundations of graph theory.

ja: √2が分数で表せないことを明かしたピタゴラス派の学者ヒッパソスが、海で死んだという伝説がある。
easy: There is an old story that a Greek thinker died at sea because he told a secret about a number.
std: Legend says Hippasus, a Pythagorean, drowned at sea after revealing that the square root of 2 cannot be written as a fraction.

ja: ロシアは世界最大の国で、日本の約45倍の広さ。11の時間帯があり、東と西の端では10時間の時差がある。
easy: Russia is the biggest country in the world. It is about 45 times as big as Japan and has 11 time zones.
std: Russia, the world's largest country, is about 45 times the size of Japan and spans 11 time zones.

ja: インドネシアは約1万7000の島からなる。人口は世界4位。
easy: Indonesia is made up of about 17,000 islands. It has the fourth most people in the world.
std: Indonesia consists of about 17,000 islands and has the world's fourth-largest population.

ja: マリアナ海溝の最も深い所（チャレンジャー海淵）は約1万900m。エベレストを沈めても2000mほど余る。
easy: The deepest part of the sea is about 11,000 meters deep. Even Mount Everest would be under water there.
std: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is nearly 11,000 meters deep; Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2,000 meters to spare.

ja: エベレストは、インドのプレートがユーラシアのプレートを押し続けているため、毎年数cmずつ北東へ動いている。
easy: Mount Everest moves a few centimeters every year, because the land under India is still pushing into Asia.
std: Mount Everest shifts a few centimeters each year as the Indian plate keeps pushing into the Eurasian plate.

ja: 南極の氷がすべてとけると、世界の海面は約58m上がると推定されている。
easy: If all the ice on Antarctica melted, the sea would rise by about 58 meters.
std: If all of Antarctica's ice melted, global sea level would rise by about 58 meters.

ja: サハラ砂漠は世界最大の暑い砂漠だが、砂におおわれているのは一部だけ。多くは岩や小石の大地。
easy: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert in the world. But most of it is rock and stones, not sand.
std: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth, yet only about a quarter of it is covered by sand; most is rock and gravel.

ja: 日本の国土の広さは世界60位前後だが、排他的経済水域（EEZ）は世界でも上位の広さがある。
easy: Japan is not a very big country, but the sea area it controls is one of the biggest in the world.
std: Japan ranks only around 60th in land area, but its exclusive economic zone at sea is among the largest in the world.

ja: 東京を中心とする首都圏の人口は約3700万人。長く世界最大の都市圏とされてきた。
easy: About 37 million people live in and around Tokyo. For many years it was called the biggest city area in the world.
std: Greater Tokyo is home to about 37 million people and has long been ranked the world's most populous metropolitan area.

ja: 地球の淡水の約7割は氷河や氷床として凍っている。すぐに使える淡水は、地球の水全体の1%にも満たない。
easy: Most of the Earth's fresh water is ice. Less than one percent of all water is fresh water we can easily use.
std: About 70% of Earth's fresh water is locked in ice, and less than 1% of all water on the planet is fresh water readily available to us.

ja: アイスランドは国土の約1割が氷河におおわれているが、活火山もたくさんある。「火と氷の国」と呼ばれる。
easy: Iceland has a lot of ice and also many active volcanoes. People call it the land of fire and ice.
std: About a tenth of Iceland is covered by glaciers, yet the island also has many active volcanoes, earning it the name 'land of fire and ice'.

ja: アフリカ大陸は、アメリカ・中国・インドを合わせたより広い。よく使われる地図では実際より小さく見える。
easy: Africa is bigger than the US, China and India put together. Many maps make it look smaller than it is.
std: Africa is larger than the United States, China and India combined, but the common Mercator map makes it look much smaller.

ja: 日本の海岸線は約3万kmあり、世界でも有数の長さ。たくさんの島があるため。
easy: Japan has about 30,000 km of coast because it has so many islands.
std: Thanks to its thousands of islands, Japan has about 30,000 km of coastline, one of the longest in the world.

ja: ベートーヴェンは、ほとんど耳が聞こえなくなってから交響曲第9番を作曲した。
easy: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony when he could hardly hear at all.
std: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.

ja: モーツァルトは5歳で作曲を始め、35歳で亡くなるまでに600曲以上を残した。
easy: Mozart began to write music at five. He wrote more than 600 works before he died at 35.
std: Mozart began composing at five and wrote more than 600 works before his death at the age of 35.

ja: モナ・リザはたて77cm、よこ53cmの小さな絵。実物を見て小ささに驚く人が多い。
easy: The Mona Lisa is only 77 cm tall. Many visitors are surprised that it is so small.
std: The Mona Lisa measures just 77 by 53 centimeters, and many visitors are surprised by how small it is.

ja: ピカソは一生で約5万点の作品を作った（絵、彫刻、陶器、版画などを含む）。
easy: Picasso made about 50,000 works of art in his life.
std: Picasso produced an estimated 50,000 works in his lifetime, including paintings, sculptures, ceramics and prints.

ja: ピアノの正式な名前は「ピアノフォルテ（弱く・強く）」。音の強弱をつけられるのが新しかった。
easy: The piano's full name is 'pianoforte', which means 'soft-loud'. It could play both soft and loud.
std: The piano's original name, pianoforte, means 'soft-loud' in Italian, because it could play at different volumes.

ja: ジャズは19世紀末から20世紀初めに、ニューオーリンズのアフリカ系アメリカ人の社会から生まれた。
easy: Jazz began in New Orleans in the African American community about 100 years ago.
std: Jazz emerged in the African American communities of New Orleans in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

ja: バッハの作品は死後しばらく忘れられていたが、1829年にメンデルスゾーンがマタイ受難曲を演奏して再び注目された。
easy: After Bach died, many people forgot his music. It became popular again in 1829.
std: Bach's music fell out of fashion after his death until Mendelssohn revived the St Matthew Passion in 1829.

ja: ゴッホが生きている間に売れた絵は1枚だけという話が有名だが、実際にはほかにも売れていたという研究がある。
easy: People often say Van Gogh sold only one painting in his life. But he may have sold a few more.
std: It is often said Van Gogh sold only one painting during his life, but research suggests he sold a few others.

ja: 映画は1秒間に24コマの速さで撮影・上映するのが長年の標準。
easy: Most films show 24 pictures every second.
std: For about a century, the standard frame rate for cinema has been 24 frames per second.

ja: モネやルノワールら印象派の画家は公式の展覧会（サロン）になかなか選ばれず、1874年に自分たちで展覧会を開いた。
easy: The official art show in Paris did not like Monet and his friends. So in 1874, they made their own show.
std: Rejected by the official Paris Salon, Monet, Renoir and other Impressionists organized their own exhibition in 1874.

ja: 日本の浮世絵は、モネやドガなどヨーロッパの画家に大きな影響を与えた（ジャポニスム）。
easy: Japanese woodblock pictures had a big effect on painters in Europe, like Monet.
std: Japanese ukiyo-e prints strongly influenced European painters such as Monet and Degas, a trend known as Japonisme.

ja: 英語で最もよく使われる文字は「E」で全体の約13%。「Z」は0.1%にも満たない。
easy: E is the most used letter in English. Z is one of the least used.
std: E is the most common letter in English, about 13% of all letters, while Z accounts for less than 0.1%.

ja: set は英語の中でも特に意味の多い単語。辞書を引くと「置く」「決める」「沈む」「一式」など、数十もの意味が並ぶ。
easy: The word set has a lot of meanings. A dictionary lists many, like put, decide and a group of things.
std: 'Set' is one of the English words with the most meanings, from 'put' and 'decide' to 'a group of things' and the sun going down.

ja: 英語の petrichor（ペトリコール）は、雨が降ったあとの土のにおいを表すことば。
easy: 'Petrichor' is the nice smell of the ground after rain.
std: 'Petrichor' is the earthy smell produced when rain falls on dry soil.

ja: typewriter は、キーボードのいちばん上の文字の列だけで打てる、長めの英単語として有名。
easy: You can type the word 'typewriter' using only the top row of letters on a keyboard.
std: 'Typewriter' is a famously long word that can be typed using only the top row of a QWERTY keyboard.

ja: stewardesses（12文字）は、キーボードの左手側のキーだけで打てる長い英単語。
easy: You can type 'stewardesses' with only your left hand on a normal keyboard.
std: 'Stewardesses', with 12 letters, can be typed using only the left-hand side of a QWERTY keyboard.

ja: 英語は約60の国と地域で公用語になっている。
easy: English is an official language in about 60 countries.
std: English is an official language in around 60 sovereign states and many other territories.

ja: rhythm は a, e, i, o, u を1つも使わない英単語。
easy: The word 'rhythm' does not use the letters a, e, i, o or u.
std: 'Rhythm' is one of the longest common English words that contains none of the vowels a, e, i, o or u.

ja: goodbye は「God be with you（神があなたとともにありますように）」が縮まってできたことば。
easy: 'Goodbye' comes from 'God be with you'.
std: 'Goodbye' is a shortened form of the old phrase 'God be with you'.

ja: sandwich は、イギリスのサンドイッチ伯爵の名前から来た。トランプを続けながら食べるために頼んだという話がある。
easy: The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich. The story says he ate it so he could keep playing cards.
std: The sandwich is named after the 4th Earl of Sandwich, who, according to legend, asked for meat between bread so he could keep playing cards.

ja: panic（パニック）は、ギリシャ神話の牧神パンに由来する。パンが起こす突然の恐怖を表した。
easy: The word 'panic' comes from Pan, a Greek god who could make people suddenly afraid.
std: 'Panic' comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild, who was believed to cause sudden fear.

ja: 世界には約7000の言語があり、その多くが話す人を失いつつある。今世紀中に半分近くが消えるという予測もある。
easy: There are about 7,000 languages in the world. Many of them may stop being used this century.
std: About 7,000 languages are spoken today, and some experts predict that nearly half could disappear by the end of this century.

ja: ハングルは15世紀に朝鮮の世宗大王が学者たちと作った文字で、とても規則的なつくりをしている。
easy: The Korean letters, Hangul, were made in the 1400s by King Sejong and his team. They are very easy to learn.
std: Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was created in the 15th century under King Sejong and is known for its logical design.

ja: 日本語の「木漏れ日」や「わびさび」のように、英語に1語で訳せないことばはたくさんある。
easy: Some Japanese words, like 'komorebi', have no one English word with the same meaning.
std: Japanese words such as 'komorebi', sunlight filtering through leaves, have no single-word equivalent in English.

ja: クラッシェンの「インプット仮説」：今の力より少しだけ難しい内容（i+1）にたくさん触れることで言語が身につくという考え。
easy: One idea says we learn a language best by reading and hearing things that are just a little hard for us.
std: Stephen Krashen's input hypothesis holds that we acquire language by understanding input slightly beyond our current level, which he called 'i+1'.

ja: 2つの言語を長く使ってきた人は、認知症の症状が出るのが平均4〜5年遅いという研究がある。
easy: Some studies found that people who use two languages show signs of memory illness a few years later.
std: Some studies found that lifelong bilinguals showed symptoms of dementia about four to five years later than monolinguals.

ja: 学んだあとに眠ると、その記憶が定着しやすくなることが多くの研究で示されている。
easy: Sleep after study helps you keep what you learned.
std: Many studies show that sleeping after learning helps consolidate new memories.

ja: テスト効果：読み返すより、思い出す練習をしたほうが長く記憶に残る。
easy: Testing yourself helps you remember better than reading again.
std: The testing effect: practicing recall helps you remember far better over time than simply rereading.

ja: 外国語で考えると、感情に流されにくく、より合理的な判断をしやすくなるという研究がある。
easy: One study found that people make calmer choices when they think in a second language.
std: Research suggests people make more rational decisions when thinking in a foreign language, a phenomenon called the foreign-language effect.

ja: エッフェル塔は、夏の暑さで鉄がのびて最大15cmほど高くなる。
easy: The Eiffel Tower can grow up to 15 cm taller in summer, because heat makes the metal longer.
std: The Eiffel Tower can grow up to about 15 cm taller in summer as its iron expands in the heat.

ja: 空が青いのは、太陽の光のうち青い光が空気でより多く散らばるため（レイリー散乱）。夕焼けが赤いのも同じしくみ。
easy: The sky is blue because the air spreads out blue light more than other colors. The same thing makes sunsets red.
std: The sky looks blue because air scatters short blue wavelengths of sunlight more than red ones, called Rayleigh scattering; the same effect makes sunsets red.

ja: 「Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo.」は文法的に正しい英文。
easy: 'Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo' is a real English sentence.
std: 'Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo' is a grammatically correct English sentence, using the city, the animal and the verb.

ja: 辞書にのる最も長い英単語のひとつ pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis は45文字。肺の病気の名前。
easy: One of the longest words in English dictionaries has 45 letters. It is the name of a lung illness.
std: Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis, a 45-letter word for a lung disease, is one of the longest words in major English dictionaries.

ja: 地球に1時間で届く太陽のエネルギーは、人類が1年間に使うエネルギーより多い。
easy: The sun gives the Earth more energy in one hour than all people use in one year.
std: The solar energy reaching Earth in a single hour is more than all of humanity uses in a year.

ja: 約50億年後、太陽は赤色巨星になって大きくふくらみ、地球をのみこむ可能性もある。
easy: In about five billion years, the sun will grow very big. It may even swallow the Earth.
std: In about five billion years the Sun will swell into a red giant and may engulf Earth.

ja: 砂は無限にあるわけではない。建設に使える角ばった砂が足りなくなり、取り合いが起きている地域もある。
easy: We are running out of the right kind of sand for building. In some places, people fight over it.
std: Sand suitable for construction is becoming scarce, and illegal sand mining has led to conflict in some regions.

ja: 音楽を聞くと、ことば・動き・感情などにかかわる脳のいくつもの場所が同時に働く。
easy: When you listen to music, many parts of your brain work at the same time.
std: Listening to music activates many brain regions at once, including areas for language, movement and emotion.

ja: 1gの土には数億〜数十億個の細菌がすんでいる。
easy: A small spoon of soil can hold hundreds of millions of very small living things.
std: A single gram of soil can contain hundreds of millions to billions of bacteria.
